authority: PHASE-2-R5-INSTRUCTION finding 4: substring presence does not prove protocol semantics. These are structured canonical records; the prose in the design documents is a RENDERING of them, not the source.
note: The checker validates relations and ordering against these records. Six words appearing in a large document prove nothing; an ordered state machine with typed transitions can be checked.

ordering_constraint.why_rejected: would leave A holding bytes R does not name, which is a bare I-43 violation governed by nothing
ordering_constraint.why_chosen: leaves R naming a digest A lacks, a state I-44 already governs
ordering_constraint.principle: where a crash window is unavoidable, place it where an existing invariant governs the resulting state

method_combination.name: institutional
method_combination.why_special: without defvar, LET establishes LEXICAL bindings and the :record methods, compiled in a different lexical environment, would not see them at all
method_combination.why_binding_placement: a dynamic binding established by LET is in effect for the dynamic extent of the LET BODY; cleanup forms of an UNWIND-PROTECT that ENCLOSES that LET run after it has exited, so the binding would already be undone when :record methods run
method_combination.why_setf: the warrant results are computed inside the protected form and must be ASSIGNED to the already-established binding; re-binding there would recreate the placement defect

outcome_values.means: warrant group failed; no primary ran
a defeater vetoed; no primary ran
control left the protected form without reaching any of the above — an error or throw from a warrant method, a defeater, or the primary

cleanup_guarantee.claimed: UNWIND-PROTECT guarantees ENTRY into the cleanup forms on normal or non-local exit from the protected form
cleanup_guarantee.residual: ANSI provides no further protection to a cleanup form that itself performs a non-local exit; a :record method that transfers control prevents later :record methods from running
